title: Ch 1.3 · Linear Lexicon
description: A 25‑round vocabulary challenge covering slope, intercepts, equation forms, and line relationships. No solving — just the exact language of linear functions. Spot the broken definition, match terms, and sort concepts under pressure.

rounds.missExplain: Trap sprung! The statement is true. Slope is the term for steepness.
rounds.prompt: The steepness of a line is officially called its slope.
rounds.explain: Yes — slope measures steepness as rise over run.
Exactly — slope is vertical change (rise) over horizontal change (run).
rounds.sentence: The slope of a line is the ratio of the horizontal change to the vertical change.
rounds.prompt: One word breaks the definition. Tap it.
rounds.missExplain: Trap sprung! The wrong word is "horizontal". Slope = rise / run, not run / rise.
rounds.hint: Which comes first in 'rise over run'?

rounds.explain: Clean — a rising line has a positive slope.
rounds.missExplain: Almost — a falling line has negative slope; rising is positive.

rounds.explain: All matched — the four slope behaviors.

rounds.missExplain: One slipped. Perpendicular slopes multiply to $-1$; they are negative reciprocals.

rounds.prompt: Select ALL correct statements about parallel lines.
rounds.explain: Yes — parallel lines share slope, never meet, and are coplanar. They don't need the same y-intercept.

choices.label: They always have the same y-intercept

rounds.explain: Sorted! Parallel same slope, no intersection; perpendicular slopes are opposite reciprocals, meet at 90°.
rounds.missExplain: Check again — equal slopes = parallel, negative reciprocal = perpendicular.

rounds.prompt: In point-slope form, $(x_1, y_1)$ can be any point on the line.

rounds.explain: Yes — as long as the point lies on the line, the form is valid.

rounds.hint: Which axis does the y-intercept lie on?
rounds.sentence: The y-intercept is the point where a line crosses the x-axis.
rounds.prompt: One word is wrong. Tap it.
rounds.explain: Yes — y-intercept is on the y-axis; x-intercept is on the x-axis.
rounds.missExplain: Trap sprung! The wrong phrase is "x-axis". The y-intercept crosses the y-axis.
